          "definition": "Let $k$ be a field with $\\operatorname{char}(k)\\ne2$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $B:V\\times V\\to k$ be a symmetric bilinear form, not necessarily nondegenerate. As ungraded real algebras, for $p,q,n\\ge0$,\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_{p+1,q+1}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}M_2(\\mathbb R),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{n+2,0}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}M_2(\\mathbb R),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+2}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}\\mathbb H.$$\n\nThe pure-signature algebras through dimension eight are\n\n| $n$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ |\n|---:|---|---|\n| $0$ | $\\mathbb R$ | $\\mathbb R$ |\n| $1$ | $\\mathbb R\\oplus\\mathbb R$ | $\\mathbb C$ |\n| $2$ | $M_2(\\mathbb R)$ | $\\mathbb H$ |\n| $3$ | $M_2(\\mathbb C)$ | $\\mathbb H\\oplus\\mathbb H$ |\n| $4$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $5$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)\\oplus M_2(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_4(\\mathbb C)$ |\n| $6$ | $M_4(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_8(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $7$ | $M_8(\\mathbb C)$ | $M_8(\\mathbb R)\\oplus M_8(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $8$ | $M_{16}(\\mathbb R)$ | $M_{16}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n\nFor every $n\\ge0$, the pure algebras satisfy\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_{n+8,0}\\cong M_{16}(\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+8}\\cong M_{16}(\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}).$$",

        },
        {
          "id": "thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification",
          "kind": "theorem",
          "title": "Real and complex Clifford algebra classification with explicit signature",
          "deps": [

            "thm-tensor-products-commute-with-arbitrary-direct-sums",

          "justified_by": [],
          "dependency_level": 6,
          "provenance": {
            "statement": "literature-derived",

          },
          "source_path": "items/thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification.md",
          "statement": "Let $n=p+q$, let $r$ be the residue of $p-q$ modulo $8$ in $\\{0,1,\\ldots,7\\}$, and use $v^2=Q(v)1$ with signature ordered $(+^p,-^q)$. For every nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$, the real Clifford algebra is\n\n| $r$ | parity of $n$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ |\n|---:|:---:|---|\n| $0$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $1$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb R)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $2$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $3$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)$ |\n| $4$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $5$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\\mathbb H)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $6$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $7$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)$ |\n\nOnly signatures with $p,q\\ge0$ are considered; in the feasible rows the displayed exponents are nonnegative. For a nondegenerate complex quadratic form on dimension $n$, its Clifford algebra is\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_n(\\mathbb C)\\cong\\begin{cases}M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb C),&n\\text{ even},\\\\M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C),&n\\text{ odd}.\\end{cases}$$\n\nThese matrix-algebra classifications require nondegeneracy; no such classification is asserted for degenerate forms.",
          "proof_strategy": "direct",
          "page": "real-complex-clifford-classification-and-graded-products"
        },
        {
          "id": "thm-graded-clifford-modules-and-real-complex-types",
          "kind": "theorem",
          "title": "Irreducible graded Clifford modules and real, complex, and quaternionic types",
          "deps": [
            "def-real-quaternion-matrix-algebra-notation",
            "def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product",
            "def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space",

            "thm-reals-ordered-field",
            "thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field",

          ],
          "justified_by": [],
          "dependency_level": 7,
          "provenance": {
            "statement": "literature-derived",
            "proof": "ai-altered"
          },
          "source_path": "items/thm-graded-clifford-modules-and-real-complex-types.md",
          "statement": "Let $A=\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ be a positive-dimensional standard real Clifford algebra with the canonical grading from [[lem-clifford-quotient-has-canonical-z2-grading]], and write $A^0$ for its even subalgebra. If $p>0$ then $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{q,p-1}$, and if $p=0$ then $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,q-1}$. For the standard complex Clifford algebra in dimension $n>0$, $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n-1}(\\mathbb C)$. Here an irreducible graded module means a nonzero graded module with no proper nonzero graded submodule ([[def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product]]). Its isomorphism class, with parity-preserving maps, is exactly the class of a simple left $A^0$-module under the induction correspondence of [[thm-graded-module-classification-from-even-subalgebra]].\n\nConsequently, if the applicable even-algebra entry in [[thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification]] is $M_m(D)$, there is one irreducible graded module with even part the column module $D^m$; if it is $M_m(D)\\oplus M_m(D)$, there are two, one supported on each factor. Their coefficient type is $D\\in\\{\\mathbb R,\\mathbb C,\\mathbb H\\}$. In complex scalars the type is always $\\mathbb C$. At dimension zero, the algebra is purely even and has two irreducible graded modules, concentrated in parity $0$ and parity $1$, respectively.\n\nFor standard complex $\\mathrm{Cl}_n(\\mathbb C)$ with $n=2m>0$, the normalized volume element $\\omega=i^m e_1\\cdots e_n$ has square $1$, lies in the even subalgebra, and anticommutes with every odd generator. The two graded-module classes are the two choices of which $\\omega$-eigenspace is placed in parity $0$; these are the two chiral parity conventions. For $n=2m+1$, the same formula gives an odd central element with square $1$; its two central idempotents are exchanged by the grading, so the two ungraded simple factors pair into the unique graded-simple class.",
          "proof_strategy": "direct",
          "page": "real-complex-clifford-classification-and-graded-products"
        }

          "title": "Filtered Taylor maps extend to the completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra",
          "deps": [
            "def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism",

          ],
          "dependency_level": 7,
          "statement": "Let $f:W\\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]], and put $P=F^1W$, $P'=F^1Z$. On $C(P)=\\bigoplus_{n\\ge0}S^nP$, including $S^0P=k\\cdot1$, use the symmetric multiplication and the counital coproduct\n\n$$\\Delta(x_1\\cdots x_n)=\\sum_{I\\sqcup J=\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}}\\epsilon(I,J;x)x_I\\otimes x_J.$$\n\nEmpty subsets are allowed. Define $\\mathcal F^NC(P)$ as the span of products $x_1\\cdots x_n$ with $x_j\\in F^{i_j}W$, all $i_j\\ge1$, and $\\sum_j i_j\\ge N$; scalars have weight zero. Define the **completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra**\n\n$$\\widehat C(P)=\\varprojlim_N C(P)/\\mathcal F^NC(P).$$\n\nAll completions and limits are degreewise. Complete tensor products for coproducts with the sum of the two weight filtrations. Then multiplication, coproduct, counit and coaugmentation extend continuously, as do $Q$ and the Taylor map $F$. Their continuous extensions satisfy $Q^2=0$, $\\Delta F=(F\\widehat\\otimes F)\\Delta$, and $FQ=RF$. The length-one projection extends continuously to $p_P:\\widehat C(P)\\to P$.\n\nFor $w\\in P^0$ and homogeneous $v\\in F^pW$, $p\\ge1$, define the convergent expressions\n\n$$e^w=\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\frac{w^n}{n!},\\qquad c_q(w)=\\sum_{n\\ge1}\\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!},\\qquad u=f_*(w)=\\sum_{n\\ge1}\\frac{f_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$\n\nThey satisfy\n\n$$\\Delta e^w=e^w\\otimes e^w,\\qquad e^we^{-w}=1,\\qquad Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w,\\qquad F(e^w)=e^u,$$\n\nand the marked-input identity\n\n$$F(ve^w)=\\left(\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\frac{f_{n+1}(w^n,v)}{n!}\\right)e^u.$$\n\nThis is a total filtration weight completion on the positive-filtration subalgebra, not an unspecified product by symmetric arity on all of $W$."

          "statement": "A **finite-field hereditary Hall category** is a supplied small\n$\\mathbb F_q$-linear abelian category $\\mathcal A$ with the following\nproperties:\n\n1.           "justified_by": [

          "statement": "A homotopy type $X$ is **locally finite** if every homotopy group $\\pi_i(X,x)$ is finite for every point $x$, and for each $x$ there is an integer $n_x$ such that $\\pi_i(X,x)=0$ for $i>n_x$.\n\nWrite $\\pi_0(X)$ for the set of connected components. Let $\\mathbb Q_c(X)$ be the rational-valued functions on $\\pi_0(X)$ with finite support. For a component $x$, the **homotopy weight** is\n$$\nw_X(x):=\\prod_{i>0}|\\pi_i(X,x)|^{(-1)^i}.\n$$\nThe product is finite because the positive homotopy groups vanish in high degrees; a negative exponent means a reciprocal.\n\nFor a map $f:X\\to Y$ of locally finite homotopy types and $\\alpha\\in\\mathbb Q_c(X)$, define\n$$\nf_!(\\alpha)(y):=\\sum_{x\\in\\pi_0(F_y)}\\alpha(i_y(x))\\,w_{F_y}(x),\n$$\nwhere $F_y$ is the homotopy fiber of $f$ at $y$ ([[def-homotopy-fiber-of-a-map]]) and $i_y:F_y\\to X$ is its natural map. For a proper map, meaning one whose homotopy fibers have finitely many connected components, also define $f^*:\\mathbb Q_c(Y)\\to\\mathbb Q_c(X)$ by $f^*\\beta=\\beta\\circ\\pi_0(f)$.\n\nThe ratio lemma [[lem-homotopy-fiber-component-weight-ratio]] proves that fibers of maps between locally finite homotopy types are locally finite and that the displayed sum is finite.           "source_path": "items/def-a1-nakajima-framed-quiver-data.md",
          "statement": "Let $Q$ be the quiver with one vertex and no arrows. Its diagram is\n\n```tikz\n\\begin{tikzpicture}\n  \\node[circle,draw,inner sep=2.5pt] at (0,0) {$\\bullet$};\n\\end{tikzpicture}\n```\n\nFor framing space $W=\\mathbb C$ and dimension $v\\in\\{0,1\\}$, put\n$V_v=\\mathbb C^v$. A **framed datum** is a pair of complex-linear maps\n$I:W\\to V_v$ and $J:V_v\\to W$, subject to the moment equation\n$I\\circ J=0\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(V_v)$. The two framing maps are\ndrawn separately from the arrows of $Q$:\n\n```tikz\n\\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth]\n  \\node (w) at (0,0) {$W=\\mathbb C$};\n  \\node (v) at (3,0) {$V_v$};\n  \\draw[->] (w) to[bend left=22] node[above] {$I$} (v);\n  \\draw[->] (v) to[bend left=22] node[below] {$J$} (w);\n\\end{tikzpicture}\n```\n\nThe group $G_v=\\operatorname{GL}(V_v)$ of invertible complex-linear maps acts\nby $g\\cdot(I,J)=(gI,Jg^{-1})$. Fix the positive real stability parameter\n$\\zeta_R>0$ and, for this one-vertex quiver, call a solution **stable** when\n$J$ is injective. Give the stable solution set its usual complex topology and\ndefine $\\mathfrak M(v,1)$ to be its quotient topological space by $G_v$.\n\nFor $v=0$ the solution set is a point, with coordinate algebra\n$A_0=\\mathbb C$; for $v=1$, writing $I(w)=iw$ and $J(z)=jz$, it is the\naffine algebraic set $ij=0$ with coordinate algebra\n$A_1=\\mathbb C[i,j]/(ij)$. These are $\\mathbb C$-algebras in the sense of\n[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]. The action on data induces an action\non each $A_v$; write $A_v^{G_v}$ for its invariant subring of fixed elements.\nDefine $\\mathfrak M_0(v,1)=\\operatorname{Spec}(A_v^{G_v})$ using\n[[def-affine-scheme-spectrum]]. An orbit of stable data maps to the point\nwhose prime ideal consists of invariant functions vanishing on that orbit;\nthis is the quotient map $\\pi_v:\\mathfrak M(v,1)\\to\\mathfrak M_0(v,1)$.\nLet $0$ denote the point induced by the zero datum and put\n$\\mathcal L(v,1)=\\pi_v^{-1}(0)$.\n\nLet $S$ be the unframed simple datum with one-dimensional vertex space and\nzero framing maps. A framed subdatum with vertex space $V'=0$ uses the same\nframing space $W$ and zero maps $I':W\\to0$ and $J':0\\to W$. Its inclusion\nuses the identity on $W$ and the unique map $\\xi:0\\to V_1$, compatible with\nthe data by $I=\\xi I'$ and $J'=J\\xi$; hence it forces $I=0$, while the\nrestriction of $J$ to $0$ is automatically zero. The quotient has framing\nspace $0$ and vertex space $V_1$, so its induced framing maps vanish and it is\n$S$. The **Hecke correspondence** $P_{0,1}$ is the locus of pairs in\n$\\mathfrak M(0,1)\\times\\mathfrak M(1,1)$ obtained this way. Its two projection\nmaps are the source and target maps of the correspondence.\n\nThe degree-zero homology of a point is $\\mathbb C$ with its point class,\nusing [[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]] and\n[[thm-singular-homology-satisfies-dimension-and-arbitrary-additivity]]. When\n$P_{0,1}$ and both spaces are points and the projections are identities,\ndefine its fundamental-class correspondence map to send the source point\nclass to the target point class; the reverse map uses the same rule. This is\nthe point push-pull convention used here."

          "source_path": "items/def-hall-algebra-module.md",
          "statement": "Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit\n([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $H$ be a unital associative\n$R$-algebra. An **$R$-linear representation of $H$** on an $R$-module $M$ is\na unital $R$-algebra homomorphism\n$\\rho:H\\to\\operatorname{End}_R(M)$, where $\\operatorname{End}_R(M)$ is the\nring of $R$-linear maps $M\\to M$, with composition as multiplication,\n$\\operatorname{id}_M$ as unit, and scalar map $r\\mapsto r\\operatorname{id}_M$.\nIt defines the unital left action\n$h\\cdot m:=\\rho(h)(m)$; its module axioms are those of\n[[def-left-and-right-modules]]. When $H$ is a Hall algebra, this structure is\ncalled a **Hall-algebra module**.\n\nThis term does not mean an object of the input category. An input object $A$\ncontributes a basis symbol $[A]$ to a Hall algebra, but that symbol by itself\nspecifies no representation on an $R$-module. The untwisted Hall algebra\ninstance is supplied by\n[[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]],\n[[thm-untwisted-hall-algebra-is-associative-and-unital]].\n\nThe zero $R$-module is allowed; its identity endomorphism is its zero map.\nThis definition gives an algebra action only. An action on a tensor product\nrequires additional structure, such as a specified coproduct."

          "statement": "Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver over a field $k$. A representation\nof $Q$ assigns a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V_i$ to each vertex\n$i\\in Q_0$ and a linear map $V_{s(a)}\\to V_{t(a)}$ to each arrow\n$a\\in Q_1$. Its dimension vector is\n$\\mathbf d=(\\dim V_i)_{i\\in Q_0}\\in\\mathbb N^{Q_0}$.\n\nFor $\\mathbf d\\in\\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ put\n$$\\operatorname{Rep}_{\\mathbf d}(Q) =\\prod_{a\\in Q_1}\\operatorname{Hom}_k (k^{d_{s(a)}},k^{d_{t(a)}}),\\qquad G_{\\mathbf d}=\\prod_{i\\in Q_0}\\operatorname{GL}_{d_i}(k),$$and let $\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d}(Q)=[\\operatorname{Rep}_{\\mathbf d}(Q)/ G_{\\mathbf d}]$ be the quotient Artin stack. It is finite type and has affine stabilizers: the representation variety and the acting group are finite type and affine, and each stabilizer is a closed subgroup of $G_{\\mathbf d}$. For dimension vectors $\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e$, let $\\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}(Q)$ be the stack of short exact sequences of representations$$0\\longrightarrow B_{\\mathbf e}\\longrightarrow E_{\\mathbf d+\\mathbf e} \\longrightarrow A_{\\mathbf d}\\longrightarrow0.$$The endpoints are part of the data, and isomorphisms are isomorphisms of the whole exact sequence. Equivalently, after choosing the standard $\\mathbf e$-dimensional subspaces at each vertex, this is the quotient by the product parabolic preserving those subspaces of the affine space of block upper-triangular arrow maps. Thus $\\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}(Q)$ is a finite-type Artin stack with affine stabilizers. More explicitly, on a local splitting $E_i=B_i\\oplus A_i$, the arrow $a:i\\to j$ has block matrix$$\\begin{pmatrix} B_a & \\xi_a\\\\ 0 & A_a \\end{pmatrix}, \\qquad \\xi_a:A_i\\to B_j.$$Changing the splitting by $h_i:A_i\\to B_i$ changes $\\xi_a$ to $\\xi_a+B_a h_i-h_j A_a$. This is the translation action of the vector bundle $\\bigoplus_i\\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_i)$ on $\\bigoplus_{a:i\\to j}\\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,B_j)$ used in the extension stack calculation. Let $q:\\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}\\to\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d}$ send a sequence to its quotient, $s:\\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}\\to \\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf e}$ send it to its subrepresentation, and $m:\\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}\\to\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d+\\mathbf e}$ send it to its middle representation. The Hall correspondence is\n\n~~~tikzcd\n& \\mathfrak E_{\\mathbf d,\\mathbf e}(Q) \\ar[dl,\"(q,s)\"'] \\ar[dr,\"m\"] & \\\\ \\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d}(Q)\\times\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf e}(Q) && \\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d+\\mathbf e}(Q)\n~~~\n\nIts arrows record the ordered quotient, subrepresentation, and middle object of the displayed short exact sequence; the diagram fixes the convolution convention. Define$$H_Q:=\\bigoplus_{\\mathbf d\\in\\mathbb N^{Q_0}} \\mathscr K(\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d}(Q)).$$For $\\alpha\\in\\mathscr K(\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d})$ and $\\beta\\in\\mathscr K(\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf e})$, define$$\\alpha*\\beta :=m_!\\big((q,s)^*(\\alpha\\boxtimes\\beta)\\big) \\in\\mathscr K(\\mathfrak M_{\\mathbf d+\\mathbf e}).$$\nThus the first factor is the quotient and the second factor is the\nsubrepresentation, so the sequence is\n$0\\to B\\to E\\to A\\to0$. Each homogeneous product is defined by one\nfinite-type stack correspondence; no completion or finiteness of a sum over\nisomorphism classes is required.           "justified_by": [],
          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion.md",
          "statement": "For $0\\le k\\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\\sum_w Q^{\\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\\in\\mathbb Z[T]$ such that\n\n$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$\n\nIt agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.\n\nFor a field $K$, $\\delta\\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\\ell$, and $p=\\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\\delta)$ for $0\\le k\\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\\ell=\\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\\ge1$ and $1\\le a<p$; if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.",
          "dependency_level": 1
        },
        {
          "id": "lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-representation-is-split-injective",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "The integral two-letter Temperley–Lieb representation has a linear left inverse",

          "justified_by": [],
          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-representation-is-split-injective.md",
          "statement": "Put $A=\\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $\\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$, let $V_n$ be the free $R$-module on binary words of length $n$, with $V_0=R$. The cup and cap maps are\n\n$$c(1)=q(01)+(10),\\qquad b(01)=1,\\quad b(10)=q^{-1},\\quad b(00)=b(11)=0.$$\n\nInsertion of these maps in adjacent positions defines a representation\n\n$$\\rho_n:\\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\\delta)\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{End}_R(V_n).$$\n\nOver $A$ this map has an $A$-linear left inverse, and the same left inverse works after every base change to $R$. In particular, it is injective over every such $R$. It preserves the number of ones, and on the local ordered basis $00,01,10,11$ the generator $d_i$ has zero $00,11$ blocks and middle block\n\n$$\\begin{pmatrix}q&1\\\\1&q^{-1}\\end{pmatrix}.$$\n\nHorizontal reflection of an endomorphism diagram is represented by matrix transpose.",
          "dependency_level": 3
        },

          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-quantum-binomial-criterion-over-fields.md",
          "statement": "Let $K$ be a field, $\\delta\\in K$, and $n\\ge0$. A normalized idempotent $e\\in\\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\\delta)$ with $d_ie=0$ for $1\\le i<n$ exists if and only if every $B_{n,k}(\\delta)$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]], $0\\le k\\le n$, is nonzero. Every such $e$ also satisfies $ed_i=0$ and is unique. This is a field assertion; it makes no integral-ring descent claim.",

          "title": "Spencer's quantum-characteristic criterion for Jones–Wenzl existence",
          "deps": [

            "lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion"
          ],
          "justified_by": [],
          "dependency_level": 5,
          "statement": "Let $K$ be a field, $\\delta\\in K$, let $\\ell$ be the quantum characteristic from [[def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic]], and let $p=\\operatorname{char}K$ (write $p=\\infty$ in characteristic zero). A normalized idempotent $e\\in\\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\\delta)$ satisfying $\\varepsilon(e)=1$ and $d_i e=0$ for every $1\\le i<n$ exists exactly in the following cases:\n\n1. if $\\ell=\\infty$, every finite $n$ satisfies the criterion $n<\\ell$;\n2. if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p$ is finite, then $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\,p(i)-1$ for some $i\\ge1$ and integer $1\\le a<p$;\n3. if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p=\\infty$, then $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell-1$ for some positive integer $a$.\n\nThe criterion is over fields.           "statement": "Fix an integer $\\ell\\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\\pi i/\\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\\ell$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\\rm target}=KE_{\\rm lib}$, $F_{\\rm target}=F_{\\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\\rm target}=K_{\\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.\n\nThe Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue.           "statement": "Let $\\ell\\ge3$. The path graph $A_{\\ell-1}$ has vertex set $\\{0,1,\\ldots,\\ell-2\\}$ and an edge between $a$ and $b$ exactly when $|a-b|=1$. For $n\\ge0$ and a vertex $a$, let $\\mathsf P_{n,a}$ be the set of sequences\n$$\np=(a_0,a_1,\\ldots,a_n)\n$$\nwith $a_0=0$, $a_n=a$, each $a_j\\in\\{0,1,\\ldots,\\ell-2\\}$, and $|a_j-a_{j-1}|=1$ for $1\\le j\\le n$. The set is finite; it may be empty. Let $V_{n,a}:=\\mathbb C^{(\\mathsf P_{n,a})}$ be the free complex vector space with basis $\\{|p\\rangle:p\\in\\mathsf P_{n,a}\\}$, and put\n$$\nK_n:=\\bigoplus_{a=0}^{\\ell-2}\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(V_{n,a}),\n$$\nomitting zero summands. For $p,q\\in\\mathsf P_{n,a}$, the matrix unit $E^{(n,a)}_{p,q}$ sends $|q\\rangle$ to $|p\\rangle$, sends every other path basis vector to zero, and is zero on every endpoint block other than $a$.\n\nEquip each $V_{n,a}$ with the Hermitian inner product for which its path basis is orthonormal, and equip each endomorphism algebra with the corresponding adjoint. Thus $(E^{(n,a)}_{p,q})^*=E^{(n,a)}_{q,p}$, and $K_n$ has the componentwise involution.\n\nFor $b\\sim a$, write $pb=(a_0,\\ldots,a_n,b)$ for the path obtained by appending $b$. Define the unital algebra map candidate $\\iota_n:K_n\\to K_{n+1}$ on matrix units by\n$$\n\\iota_n(E^{(n,a)}_{p,q})=\\sum_{b\\sim a}E^{(n+1,b)}_{pb,qb},\n$$\nand extend it linearly. The next local theorem proves that these assignments are injective unital $*$-homomorphisms and gives the corresponding branching rule.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf\nsuppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine\nalgebraic group, $B\\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,\n$X=G/B$, $\\mathfrak g=\\operatorname{Lie}G$,\n$\\mathfrak h=\\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by\n$B$. For an integral weight $\\eta$, $\\mathcal O_X(\\eta)$ denotes the\n$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\\times^B\\mathbb C_\\eta$ with fiber character\n$\\eta$ at $eB$.\n\nThe infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor\n$$a_X:\\mathcal L_X:=\\mathcal O_X\\otimes_{\\mathbb C}\\mathfrak g\\longrightarrow T_X,\\qquad f\\otimes x\\longmapsto f x_X.$$\nGive $\\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket\n$$[f\\otimes x,g\\otimes y]=fg\\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\\otimes y-g y_X(f)\\otimes x.$$\nIts kernel $\\mathfrak b_X=\\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at\n$gB$ its fiber is $\\operatorname{Ad}(g)\\mathfrak b$.\n\nFor any $\\kappa\\in\\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\\kappa+\\rho$ of\n$\\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an\n$\\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\\chi^X_{\\kappa+\\rho}:\\mathfrak b_X\\to\\mathcal O_X$.\nThe transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a\ncharacter is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid\nenveloping sheaf $\\mathcal U_X(\\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\\mathcal O_X$\nand $\\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and\n$$[x,f]=x_X(f),\\qquad x\\in\\mathcal L_X,\\ f\\in\\mathcal O_X.$$\nDefine the sheaf of twisted differential operators\n$$\\mathcal D_\\kappa:=\\mathcal U_X(\\mathfrak g)/\\bigl(\\xi-\\chi^X_{\\kappa+\\rho}(\\xi):\\xi\\in\\mathfrak b_X\\bigr).$$\nIts order filtration assigns order zero to $\\mathcal O_X$ and order at most\none to the image of $\\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered\n$\\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\\mathcal O_X$, associated graded\n$\\operatorname{Sym}_{\\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to\nthe anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\\mathcal D_\\kappa$\nare proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left\n$\\mathcal D_\\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an\n$\\mathcal O_X$-module.\n\nFor $z\\in Z(U(\\mathfrak g))$, let $\\operatorname{pr}(z)\\in U(\\mathfrak h)$ be\nthe Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and\nput\n$$\\chi_\\kappa(z)=\\operatorname{pr}(z)(\\kappa-\\rho).$$\nThis is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it\n$W$-invariant in $\\kappa$. Define\n$$A_\\kappa=U(\\mathfrak g)/U(\\mathfrak g)\\ker\\chi_\\kappa.$$\nThe regularity convention is **antidominant** when\n$\\langle\\kappa,\\alpha^\\vee\\rangle\\notin\\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive\nroot $\\alpha$, and **regular** when\n$\\langle\\kappa,\\alpha^\\vee\\rangle\\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights,\n$\\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary\ncomplex numbers is used.",

          "dependency_level": 2,
          "statement": "Let $\\alpha$ be a simple root, $P_\\alpha$ its minimal parabolic,\n$Y=G/P_\\alpha$, and $p_\\alpha:X=G/B\\to Y$. Let\n$\\kappa\\in\\mathfrak h^*$ satisfy $\\langle\\kappa,\\alpha^\\vee\\rangle=0$.\nThe restriction of $\\kappa$ to $\\mathfrak p_\\alpha$ that is zero on root\nspaces is a Lie algebra character.           "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "Let $R=(X,\\Phi,Y,\\Phi^\\vee,\\Delta)$ be a reduced based root datum: $X,Y$ are finite-rank free lattices in perfect integral duality, $\\Phi\\subset X$ is the finite root set, $\\Phi^\\vee\\subset Y$ its coroot set, $\\Delta$ a base, and $W_0$ the finite Weyl group ([[def-abstract-root-datum-and-its-weyl-group]]). Its finite simple-reflection set is $S_0:=\\{s_\\alpha:\\alpha\\in\\Delta\\}\\subset W_0$; the simple reflections in a chosen base generate $W_0$ ([[lem-root-datum-combinatorics]]).           "id": "def-separable-algebra-and-bimodule-in-fusion-category",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Separable algebra objects and bimodules in a fusion category",
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "deps": [

          "statement": "In a monoidal category $\\mathcal C$, an **algebra object** is an object $A$ with multiplication $m_A:A\\otimes A\\to A$ and unit $\\eta_A:\\mathbf1\\to A$ satisfying associativity and unit equations with the associator and unitors of $\\mathcal C$. It is **separable** if there is an $A$-bimodule morphism $\\sigma_A:A\\to A\\otimes A$ with $m_A\\sigma_A=1_A$. The composite $e_A=\\sigma_A\\eta_A:\\mathbf1\\to A\\otimes A$ is its **separability element**. It satisfies $m_Ae_A=\\eta_A$ and the centrality equation\n$$ (m_A\\otimes1_A)\\circ(1_A\\otimes e_A)=(1_A\\otimes m_A)\\circ(e_A\\otimes1_A):A\\longrightarrow A\\otimes A,$$\nwith associators inserted. In element notation these are $\\sum_i x_i y_i=1_A$ and $\\sum_i a x_i\\otimes y_i=\\sum_i x_i\\otimes y_i a$.\n\nA **left $A$-module** is an object $M\\in\\mathcal C$ with an associative unital action $l_M:A\\otimes M\\to M$; a **right $A$-module** has an associative unital action $r_M:M\\otimes A\\to M$. Write $\\operatorname{Mod}^{l}_{\\mathcal C}(A)$ and $\\operatorname{Mod}^{r}_{\\mathcal C}(A)$ for their categories and module morphisms. The category of left $A$-modules is a right $\\mathcal C$-module category by $M\\odot X:=M\\otimes X$, with left $A$-action obtained by associating $A\\otimes(M\\otimes X)$ to $(A\\otimes M)\\otimes X$ and applying $l_M\\otimes1_X$, and the inherited associator and unitor. An **$A$-$B$ bimodule** is an object $X\\in\\mathcal C$ with commuting left and right actions $A\\otimes X\\to X$ and $X\\otimes B\\to X$, each associative and unital. A bimodule morphism preserves both actions.\n\nThe **regular $A$-$A$ bimodule** is the object $A$ with both actions given by $m_A$.\n\nGiven an $A$-$B$ bimodule $X$ and a $B$-$D$ bimodule $Y$, a morphism $q:X\\otimes Y\\to Z$ is **balanced over $B$** if\n$$q\\circ(r_X\\otimes1_Y)=q\\circ(1_X\\otimes l_Y):X\\otimes B\\otimes Y\\longrightarrow Z.$$\nA relative tensor product $X\\otimes_B Y$, when it exists, is an object with a balanced map $q_B:X\\otimes Y\\to X\\otimes_B Y$ universal among balanced maps.           "statement": "Fix a field $k$. A **weak linear 2-category** $\\mathcal B$ consists of a class of objects and, for each ordered pair $(A,B)$, a $k$-linear category $\\mathcal B(A,B)$. Its objects are called **1-morphisms** and its morphisms are called **2-morphisms**. Each triple $A,B,C$ has a $k$-bilinear composition functor\n$$\\mathcal B(B,C)\\times\\mathcal B(A,B)\\longrightarrow\\mathcal B(A,C),\\qquad (g,f)\\longmapsto g\\circ f,$$\nand each $A$ has an identity 1-morphism $1_A\\in\\mathcal B(A,A)$. A $k$-linear category here means that every hom set is a $k$-vector space and composition is bilinear.\n\nFor composable $f:A\\to B$, $g:B\\to C$, and $h:C\\to D$, there is a natural invertible 2-morphism\n$$a_{h,g,f}:(h\\circ g)\\circ f\\Longrightarrow h\\circ(g\\circ f).$$\nFor each $f:A\\to B$ there are natural invertible unit 2-morphisms\n$$\\ell_f:1_B\\circ f\\Longrightarrow f,\\qquad r_f:f\\circ1_A\\Longrightarrow f.$$\nThe associators satisfy the pentagon equation on every fourfold composite; the two unitors and associator satisfy the triangle equation on every pair of composable 1-morphisms. These equations are equalities of 2-morphisms between the indicated parallel 1-morphisms. Vertical composition is composition in each hom category. Horizontal composition is the displayed functor, so functoriality gives the interchange equation between horizontal and vertical composition.\n\nWhen the associators and unitors are identities, this is a strict 2-category in the sense of [[def-strict-two-category]]. No strictness is imposed in the weak definition.",

          "statement": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over an algebraically closed field.           "kind": "definition",

          "statement": "Let $\\mathcal B$ be a weak linear $2$-category. A **monad on $A$ in $\\mathcal B$** is a $1$-morphism $T:A\\to A$ with $2$-morphisms $\\eta:1_A\\Rightarrow T$ and $\\mu:T\\circ T\\Rightarrow T$ satisfying\n$$\\mu\\cdot(\\mu\\ast1_T)=\\mu\\cdot(1_T\\ast\\mu),\\qquad \\mu\\cdot(\\eta\\ast1_T)=1_T=\\mu\\cdot(1_T\\ast\\eta),$$\nwhere $\\cdot$ is vertical composition, $\\ast$ is horizontal composition, and the associator and unitors of $\\mathcal B$ are inserted. Equivalently it is an algebra object in the monoidal endomorphism category $\\mathcal B(A,A)$. This extends the ordinary-category definition in [[def-monad]]. It is **separable** if there is a $2$-morphism $\\sigma:T\\Rightarrow T\\circ T$ with\n$$\\mu\\cdot\\sigma=1_T,\\qquad \\sigma\\cdot\\mu=(\\mu\\ast1_T)\\cdot(1_T\\ast\\sigma)=(1_T\\ast\\mu)\\cdot(\\sigma\\ast1_T),$$\nagain with coherent associators. The last two equalities say that $\\sigma$ is a map of regular $T$-bimodules.\n\nAn **adjunction** $L\\dashv U$ in $\\mathcal B$, for $L:A\\to B$ and $U:B\\to A$, consists of $2$-morphisms $\\eta:1_A\\Rightarrow UL$ and $\\varepsilon:LU\\Rightarrow1_B$ with\n$$(\\varepsilon\\ast1_L)\\cdot(1_L\\ast\\eta)=1_L,\\qquad(1_U\\ast\\varepsilon)\\cdot(\\eta\\ast1_U)=1_U,$$\nwith associators and unitors inserted. These are the same triangle equations as in [[def-adjunction-by-unit-counit-and-triangle-identities]], now for $1$- and $2$-morphisms of $\\mathcal B$. Its induced monad is $(UL,\\eta,1_U\\ast\\varepsilon\\ast1_L)$.\n\nA **finite semisimple linear 2-category** is a weak linear 2-category in which:\n\n- every hom category is a finite semisimple $k$-linear category (it has finitely many simple isomorphism classes, finite-dimensional hom spaces, and every object is a finite direct sum of simples);\n- there is a zero object, and each pair $A,B$ has a biproduct $A\\oplus B$ with inclusions and projections $\\iota_A,\\iota_B,\\pi_A,\\pi_B$ satisfying $\\pi_i\\circ\\iota_j\\cong0$ for $i\\ne j$, $\\pi_i\\circ\\iota_i\\cong1$, and $\\iota_A\\circ\\pi_A\\oplus\\iota_B\\circ\\pi_B\\cong1_{A\\oplus B}$; finite biproducts are preserved by composition;\n- every 1-morphism has both a left and a right adjoint ([[def-adjunction-by-unit-counit-and-triangle-identities]]), with unit and counit 2-morphisms satisfying the two triangle identities;\n- every separable monad has a separable splitting: a separable monad $T:A\\to A$ is represented by an object $A_T$ and an adjunction $L\\dashv U$, where $L:A\\to A_T$ and $U:A_T\\to A$, in the sense of [[def-adjunction-by-unit-counit-and-triangle-identities]]. Its induced monad $UL$ is isomorphic to $T$ as a monad, and its counit $\\varepsilon:LU\\Rightarrow 1_{A_T}$ has a section $s:1_{A_T}\\Rightarrow LU$ as a 2-morphism in $\\mathcal B(A_T,A_T)$, with $\\varepsilon\\circ s=1_{1_{A_T}}$ (in a bimodule presentation this section is a bimodule map);\n- there are finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects, where an object $A$ is **simple** when its identity 1-morphism is simple in $\\mathcal B(A,A)$.\n\nThe splitting condition concerns monads in the 2-category; it is stronger than the existence of finite direct sums in each hom category.           "statement": "A **weak monoidal 2-category** is a weak 2-category $\\mathcal B$ together with the following data.\n\n1. A bilinear tensor pseudofunctor $\\otimes:\\mathcal B\\times\\mathcal B\\to\\mathcal B$. On 1- and 2-morphisms it has invertible comparison 2-morphisms for composition and identities, natural in each variable and satisfying the pseudofunctor composition and unit equations.\n2. A unit object $I$.\n3. Pseudonatural equivalences $a_{A,B,C}:(A\\otimes B)\\otimes C\\to A\\otimes(B\\otimes C)$ and $\\ell_A:I\\otimes A\\to A$, $r_A:A\\otimes I\\to A$.           "title": "The Frattini subgroup of a finite group is characteristic",

      "id": "frattini-subgroups-and-the-burnside-basis-theorem",
      "title": "Frattini Subgroups and the Burnside Basis Theorem",
      "kind": "A",
      "category": "group-theory",
      "companion": "frattini-subgroups-and-the-burnside-basis-theorem-examples",

      "items": [
        {
          "id": "lem-frattini-subgroup-is-characteristic",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "The Frattini subgroup of a finite group is characteristic",
          "strategy": "Every automorphism sends maximal proper subgroups to maximal proper subgroups, hence permutes the family whose intersection is $\\Phi(G)$. Taking the image of that intersection gives the same intersection. Treat the trivial group through the published empty-intersection convention.",
          "deps": [
            "def-frattini-subgroup-of-a-finite-group",
            "def-characteristic-subgroup"
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "cor-generation-is-detected-modulo-the-frattini-subgroup",
          "kind": "corollary",

- **nondecreasing** when $f(x) \le f(y)$ for all $x, y \in A$ with $x \le y$;
- **increasing**, or *strictly increasing*, when $f(x) < f(y)$ for all
  $x, y \in A$ with $x < y$;
- **nonincreasing** when $f(x) \ge f(y)$ for all $x, y \in A$ with $x \le y$;
- **decreasing**, or *strictly decreasing*, when $f(x) > f(y)$ for all
  $x, y \in A$ with $x < y$;
- **monotone** when it is nondecreasing or nonincreasing;
- **strictly monotone** when it is increasing or decreasing.

The naming follows the convention of [[def-monotone-sequence]], which is the
convention of this library throughout: *increasing* is the strict notion and
*nondecreasing* the weak one.

**An increasing function is nondecreasing, and a decreasing function is
nonincreasing.** For $x \le y$ either $x < y$, and then $f(x) < f(y)$, hence
$f(x) \le f(y)$; or $x = y$, and then $f(x) = f(y)$. The same argument with the
inequalities reversed gives the second claim. So strictly monotone implies
monotone.

**A strictly monotone function is injective**
([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]). Let $f$ be increasing and let
$x, y \in A$ with $x \ne y$. By trichotomy either $x < y$, and then
$f(x) < f(y)$, or $y < x$, and then $f(y) < f(x)$; in both cases
$f(x) \ne f(y)$. The decreasing case is the same argument. The converse fails,
and the failure is not exotic: a continuous injection on an interval *is*
strictly monotone ([[thm-continuous-injection-on-an-interval-is-strictly-monotone]]),

case to a nondecreasing one.

**Monotone on a set, not at a point.** All six conditions are conditions on the

ordered set $\mathbb{N}$ in place of the ordered subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
and with the comparison of indices in place of the comparison of arguments. So

used interchangeably: the words *nondecreasing*, *increasing*, *nonincreasing*,

$(x_k)$ is nonincreasing and $f$ is nonincreasing, then $j \le k$ gives

The witness is $f(x) = -x$ on $A = \mathbb{R}$ with $x_k = -k$, where both $f$ and

$$A^{-} := A \cap (-\infty, c), \qquad A^{+} := A \cap (c, \infty)$$

([[def-interval]]), and recall that $\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x)$ is defined only
when $c$ is a limit point of $A^{-}$, and $\lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x)$ only when
$c$ is a limit point of $A^{+}$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]).

**At an isolated point there is nothing to classify.** If $c$ is an isolated
point of $A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so that $A \cap N_{\rho}(c) = \{c\}$ for
some real $\rho > 0$, then $f$ is continuous at $c$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$

every discontinuity is a limit point of $A$, and the classification below covers
every case that occurs.

### Two-sided points

Suppose $c$ is a limit point of **both** $A^{-}$ and $A^{+}$, so that both
one-sided limits are well posed. Say that $c$ is a discontinuity

- **of the first kind** when both one-sided limits exist;
- **of the second kind**, also called **essential**, when at least one of the two
  one-sided limits fails to exist.

A discontinuity of the first kind is further

- **removable** when $\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x)$; the
  common value is then different from $f(c)$, for otherwise
  [[thm-two-sided-limit-iff-both-one-sided]] would give
  $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ and $f$ would be continuous at $c$
  ([[def-continuity-real]]);
- a **jump** when $\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x) \ne \lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x)$; the
  difference $\lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x) - \lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x)$ is then called
  the **jump of $f$ at $c$**.

exhaust the two-sided discontinuities of $f$: either both one-sided limits
exist, and then they are equal or not, or one of them does not exist.

**Removable is a name for what can be repaired.** If $c$ is a removable
discontinuity with common one-sided value $L$, then the function agreeing with

the single value $f(c)$ removes the discontinuity. No such repair is available at
a jump or at an essential discontinuity, since there the two-sided limit does not
exist at all and no choice of value at $c$ can create it.

**Oscillation on a set.** For $S \subseteq A$ put

$$\omega_f(S) \;:=\; \sup\{\, |f(x) - f(y)| \;:\; x, y \in S \,\} \;\in\; \overline{\mathbb{R}} .$$

**Oscillation at a point.** For $c \in A$ put

$$\omega_f(c) \;:=\; \inf\{\, \omega_f(A \cap N_\delta(c)) \;:\; \delta \in \mathbb{R},\ \delta > 0 \,\} \;\in\; \overline{\mathbb{R}},$$

exists, and each of its members is $\ge 0$: for $c \in A$ the set

### The Dirichlet function

$$\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{Q}} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad \mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{Q}}(x) := \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } x \in \mathbb{Q},\\ 0 & \text{if } x \notin \mathbb{Q}.\end{cases}$$

This is the indicator of the rationals. It is a function because every real
either lies in $\mathbb{Q}$ or does not, and the two clauses are exclusive.

### The least denominator of a rational

Let $x \in \mathbb{Q}$ and put

$$Q(x) \;:=\; \{\, q \in \mathbb{N} \;:\; q \ge 1 \ \text{ and } \ q\,x \in \mathbb{Z} \,\}.$$

**$Q(x)$ is nonempty.** Every rational is $a/b$ with $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $b$ a
positive integer ([[lem-int-embeds-rat]]), and a positive integer is $q$
for a unique natural $q \ge 1$ ([[lem-nat-embeds-int]]); then
$q\,x = a \in \mathbb{Z}$, so $q \in Q(x)$.

By the well-ordering principle ([[thm-well-ordering-principle]]) the nonempty
subset $Q(x) \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has a least element. Write

$$q(x) \;:=\; \min Q(x) \;\ge\; 1,$$

the **least denominator** of $x$, and $p(x) := q(x)\,x \in \mathbb{Z}$,
so that

$$x \;=\; \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} .$$

Nothing is selected here: $q(x)$ is the least element of a set determined by
$x$, so it is a function of $x$ alone.

**The least denominator is the denominator in lowest terms.** The integers
$p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are coprime ([[def-coprime]]). Indeed put
$d := \gcd(p(x), q(x))$, which satisfies $d \ge 1$ because $q(x) \ge 1$ makes the

carries products of naturals to products ([[lem-of-naturals-positive]]); hence

$$(q(x)/d)\,x \;=\; \frac{q(x)\,x}{d} \;=\; \frac{p(x)}{d} \;\in\; \mathbb{Z},$$

so $q(x)/d \in Q(x)$ and therefore $q(x)/d \ge q(x)$, which forces $d = 1$.

unambiguous.** Suppose $x = p/q$ with $q \ge 1$ a natural, $p \in \mathbb{Z}$

### The equivalent pointwise form

$f$ has the intermediate value property **if and only if**

> for all $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and every real $y$ with $f(a) \le y \le f(b)$
> or $f(b) \le y \le f(a)$, there is $c \in [a,b]$ with $f(c) = y$.

*From the displayed condition to the pointwise one.* Given $a < b$ in $I$, the
set $[a,b]$ is order-convex and contained in $I$ by order-convexity of $I$, so

$c \in J$ because $J$ is order-convex and $a, b \in J$; so $y \in f[J]$. If
$b < a$ the same argument applies with the roles of $a$ and $b$ exchanged, the

$$\Gamma \;:=\; \{\, (x, f(x)) \;:\; x \in \mathbb{R} \,\} \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{R}^{2}$$

be the graph of $f$. If **any one** of the following six conditions holds, then
$f(x) = c\,x$ for every real $x$.

1. $f$ is continuous at some single point of $\mathbb{R}$

2. $f$ is monotone on some nondegenerate interval
   ([[def-monotone-function]], [[def-interval]]).
3. $f$ is bounded above on some nondegenerate interval ([[def-bounded-set]]).
4. $f$ is bounded below on some nondegenerate interval.
5. $f$ has constant sign on some nondegenerate interval $I$: either $f(z) \ge 0$

6. $\Gamma$ is **not** dense in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
   ([[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]]).

are.** Condition 5 is the special case of 3 or of 4 with the bound $0$, and
condition 4 is condition 3 applied to $-f$; they are listed separately only
because each is the form in which the hypothesis usually arises. Condition 1 and

one that is not, and it is proved in the contrapositive: if $f$ is not of the
form $x \mapsto cx$, then $\Gamma$ is dense.

            "lem-it-finite-product-law-is-iid",
            "def-it-empirical-type-and-type-class",

            "lem-it-number-of-n-types-polynomial-bound",

            "lem-it-n-type-approximation",
            "lem-it-finite-relative-entropy-continuity-on-simplex"
          ],
          "dependency_level": 4,
          "justified_by": [],
          "statement": "Let $\\mathcal A$ be finite, let $p$ be a probability vector on $\\mathcal A$, and set $S:=\\operatorname{supp}(p)=\\{a\\in\\mathcal A:p(a)>0\\}$. Then $S$ is finite nonempty and $p(a)>0$ on $S$. For each $n\\ge1$, use the finite product law $p^{\\otimes n}$ from [[def-it-finite-alphabet-product-law]] and [[lem-it-finite-product-law-is-iid]] on $\\mathcal A^n$, and let $X_1^{(n)},\\ldots,X_n^{(n)}$ be its coordinate maps. Let $\\widehat P_n$ be the empirical type of this coordinate word, viewed as a $\\Delta(\\mathcal A)$-valued map. Identify the support simplex\n$$\\Delta(S):=\\{q\\in[0,1]^S:\\sum_{a\\in S}q(a)=1\\}$$\nwith the face of $\\Delta(\\mathcal A)$ whose coordinates outside $S$ vanish. Then $\\widehat P_n\\in\\Delta(S)$ almost surely under $p^{\\otimes n}$. For any set $\\Gamma\\subseteq\\Delta(S)$, let $\\Gamma^\\circ$ and $\\overline\\Gamma$ denote its interior and closure in the relative topology induced by $\\|\\cdot\\|_1$.\nWith $\\inf\\varnothing=+\\infty$ and $\\ln0=-\\infty$,\n$$\\liminf_{n\\to\\infty}\\frac1n\\ln p^{\\otimes n}(\\widehat P_n\\in\\Gamma)\\ge-\\inf_{q\\in\\Gamma^\\circ}D(q\\|p),$$\nand\n$$\\limsup_{n\\to\\infty}\\frac1n\\ln p^{\\otimes n}(\\widehat P_n\\in\\Gamma)\\le-\\inf_{q\\in\\overline\\Gamma}D(q\\|p).$$\nFor every $n\\ge1$ the finite upper bound\n$$p^{\\otimes n}(\\widehat P_n\\in\\Gamma)\\le(n+1)^{|S|-1}\\exp\\!\\left(-n\\inf_{q\\in\\overline\\Gamma}D(q\\|p)\\right)$$\nalso holds. If the two infima agree, the limit exists and equals their negative common value. Equivalently, when $S\\ne\\mathcal A$, one may restrict the product sample space to $S^n$ without changing these event probabilities, since every word outside $S^n$ has zero product mass."
        }
      ],
      "summary": "Define empirical types and prove type-class counting/probability bounds before the finite-alphabet Sanov large-deviation theorem.",

      "scaffold": "research/plan-information-theory-track.md",
      "order": 2504

          "id": "def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Finite discrete memoryless networks and causal codes",
          "deps": [],
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "A **finite discrete memoryless network (DMN)** has a node set $[N]=\\{1,\\ldots,N\\}$ for an integer $N\\ge1$, finite nonempty input alphabets $\\mathcal X_k$ and output alphabets $\\mathcal Y_k$, and one transition probability vector $W(y_1,\\ldots,y_N\\mid x_1,\\ldots,x_N)$ for each input tuple. At each use, conditional on the current input tuple, the output tuple is drawn from this vector independently of earlier uses.\n\nNode $k$ may have an independent uniform message $M_k$ in a finite nonempty set $\\mathcal M_k$ and a destination set $D_k\\subseteq[N]$. A length-$n$ **causal code** consists of encoders $X_{k,i}=f_{k,i}(M_k,Y_k^{i-1})$ and, for each destination $d\\in D_k$, a decoder $\\widehat M_{kd}=g_{kd}(Y_d^n,M_d)$; here $Y_k^{i-1}=(Y_{k,1},\\ldots,Y_{k,i-1})$, with the empty tuple at $i=1$. The average error is the probability that any required estimate differs from its message. A rate tuple is achievable if a sequence of such codes has error tending to zero and message-set rates tending to at least that tuple; the capacity region is the closure of achievable tuples."
        },
        {
          "id": "def-real-gaussian-multicast-relay-network",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Real scalar Gaussian multicast relay network and power constraints",
          "deps": [],
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "A **real scalar Gaussian relay network** has node set $[N]$ for an integer $N\\ge1$, source set $\\mathcal S\\subseteq[N]$, destination set $\\mathcal D\\subseteq[N]$, one real input $X_i$ and output $Y_i$ at each node, and channel equations\n$$Y_j=\\sum_{i=1}^N g_{ji}X_i+Z_j,\\qquad j\\in[N],$$\nwhere the gains $g_{ji}\\in\\mathbb R$ are fixed and the noises $Z_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables, independent across channel uses and of all source messages. At each use the current noise vector is independent of all past observations and the current inputs; future inputs may depend on past noises through feedback. Each node has a nonnegative power budget $P_i\\ge0$ and average power constraint $\\frac1n\\sum_{t=1}^n\\mathbb E[X_{i,t}^2]\\le P_i$. Each source $i\\in\\mathcal S$ has an independent uniform message $M_i$ in a finite nonempty set $\\mathcal M_i$. For every non-source node $i\\notin\\mathcal S$, set $\\mathcal M_i=\\{*\\}$ and $M_i=*$, so its encoder has no message information. A length-$n$ causal code uses measurable encoders $X_{i,t}=f_{i,t}(M_i,Y_i^{t-1})$ and destination decoders based on $(Y_d^n,M_d)$, where $M_d$ is its own source message when $d\\in\\mathcal S$ and a singleton otherwise; multicast means every destination must decode every other source message, while its own message is already known. The average error probability is the probability that any required destination estimate is wrong. Write $G_{B,A}$ for the matrix with rows indexed by $B$ and columns by $A$ whose entries are $g_{ji}$.\n\nRates in this page's Gaussian formulas are measured in bits per use, $R_i=n^{-1}\\log_2|\\mathcal M_i|$."
        },
        {
          "id": "def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Real and complex two-user Gaussian interference channels",
          "deps": [],
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "The two-user Gaussian interference channel has independent messages, separate encoders, and outputs\n$$Y_1=h_{11}X_1+h_{21}X_2+Z_1,\\qquad Y_2=h_{12}X_1+h_{22}X_2+Z_2.$$\nFor the **real model**, $X_i,h_{ji},Z_j$ are real and $Z_j\\sim N(0,1)$. For the **complex model**, the inputs and gains are complex and $Z_j\\sim\\mathcal{CN}(0,1)$ with density $\\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$. The receiver-noise variables are independent across receivers and channel uses and independent of the messages, so the channel is memoryless. Each power budget satisfies $P_i\\ge0$. A length-$n$ code has independent uniform messages $M_i$ on $[m_i]$ for integers $m_i\\ge1$, deterministic separate encoders $X_i^n=f_i(M_i)$, and decoders $\\widehat M_i=g_i(Y_i^n)$; no feedback is present. The expected average-power constraints are $n^{-1}\\sum_{t=1}^n\\mathbb E[X_{i,t}^2]\\le P_i$ in the real model and $n^{-1}\\sum_{t=1}^n\\mathbb E|X_{i,t}|^2\\le P_i$ in the complex model, with expectations under the uniform message law. The average joint error is $\\Pr\\{(\\widehat M_1,\\widehat M_2)\\ne(M_1,M_2)\\}$. For either model define\n$$\\mathrm{SNR}_1=|h_{11}|^2P_1,\\quad \\mathrm{SNR}_2=|h_{22}|^2P_2,\\quad \\mathrm{INR}_1=|h_{21}|^2P_2,\\quad \\mathrm{INR}_2=|h_{12}|^2P_1.$$\nRates are bits per use, $R_i=n^{-1}\\log_2m_i$. For a scalar unit-noise AWGN link $Y=aX+Z$ with power constraint $P$, the capacity is $\\kappa\\log_2(1+|a|^2P)$, attained by a centered real Gaussian input or a circular complex Gaussian input; $\\kappa=1/2$ in the real model and $\\kappa=1$ in the complex model."
        },

          "dependency_level": 1,
          "statement": "A **finite discrete memoryless relay channel** is the three-node instance of [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]] with source input $X\\in\\mathcal X$, relay input $X_r\\in\\mathcal X_r$, relay observation $Y_r\\in\\mathcal Y_r$, destination observation $Y\\in\\mathcal Y$, and transition law $W(y_r,y\\mid x,x_r)$. For a positive integer message-set size $M$, the one-way message is uniform on $[M]$ and the destination estimates it from $Y^n$.\n\nIn the **relay-only causal model**, $X_i=f_i(M)$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y_r^{i-1})$. In the **full output-feedback model**, both encoders know the past pair $(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$, so $X_i=f_i(M,Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$. In either model the channel outputs at time $i$ are drawn from $W(\\cdot,\\cdot\\mid X_i,X_{r,i})$; no encoder sees a current-time output before choosing its current input. The rate is $n^{-1}\\ln M$, and achievability uses average error under the uniform message law."

          "dependency_level": 1,
          "statement": "A **finite two-user interference channel** is the two-sender, two-receiver memoryless channel with finite nonempty input alphabets $\\mathcal X_1,\\mathcal X_2$, finite nonempty output alphabets $\\mathcal Y_1,\\mathcal Y_2$, and transition law $W(y_1,y_2|x_1,x_2)$. Independent uniform messages $M_1,M_2$ on finite nonempty sets are encoded separately as $X_1^n=f_1(M_1)$ and $X_2^n=f_2(M_2)$; receiver $i$ estimates $M_i$ from $Y_i^n$. The **strong-interference regime** means that, for every product law $P_{X_1}P_{X_2}$,\n$$I(X_1;Y_1|X_2)\\le I(X_1;Y_2|X_2),\\qquad I(X_2;Y_2|X_1)\\le I(X_2;Y_1|X_1).$$\nThe inequalities are evaluated under the stated product law and the channel.           "statement": "Let $A$ be a $d$-dimensional complex inner-product space with $d\\ge1$. Let $J:A\\to B$ be the isometric inclusion into the data summand.\n\nFor an erasure probability $\\epsilon\\in[0,1]$, the **$d$-dimensional quantum erasure channel** is the linear map\n\n$$\\mathcal E_{d,\\epsilon}(X):=(1-\\epsilon)JXJ^*+ \\epsilon\\operatorname{tr}(X)|e\\rangle\\langle e|,\\qquad X\\in\\mathcal L(A).$$\n\nFor a density operator $\\rho$, this outputs the data state with probability $1-\\epsilon$ and the orthogonal erasure flag with probability $\\epsilon$.           "justified_by": [],
          "dependency_level": 1,
          "statement": "Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\\mathcal N:\\mathcal L(A)\\to\\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\\to B\\otimes E$ such that\n\n$$\\mathcal N(X)=\\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$\n\nfor every $X\\in\\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel\n\n$$\\mathcal N^c(X):=\\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\\in\\mathcal L(E)$$\n\nis the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).\n\nIt is a quantum channel: reorder $B\\otimes E$ to $E\\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].\n\nFor a density operator $\\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\\psi\\rangle\\in A\\otimes R$ with $\\operatorname{Tr}_R|\\psi\\rangle\\langle\\psi|=\\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\\omega_{BR}:=(\\mathcal N\\otimes\\operatorname{id}_R)(|\\psi\\rangle\\langle\\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is\n\n$$I_c(\\rho,\\mathcal N):=S(\\mathcal N(\\rho))-S(\\omega_{BR}),$$\n\nwhere $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\\mathcal N\\otimes\\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]).           "source_path": "items/def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product.md",
          "statement": "Let $k$ be a field. A $\\mathbb Z/2$-graded $k$-vector space is a direct sum $A=A^0\\oplus A^1$; a homogeneous element $a\\in A^i$ has parity $|a|=i\\in\\{0,1\\}$. A $\\mathbb Z/2$-graded unital associative $k$-algebra is such a space with $1\\in A^0$ and $A^iA^j\\subseteq A^{i+j\\pmod 2}$. A graded left module is a module $M=M^0\\oplus M^1$ satisfying $A^iM^j\\subseteq M^{i+j\\pmod 2}$. A graded submodule is an $A$-submodule $N=N^0\\oplus N^1$; a graded-simple module is nonzero and has no proper nonzero graded submodule. An isomorphism of graded modules preserves both parity components.\n\nFor graded algebras $A,B$, their graded tensor product $A\\widehat\\otimes_k B$ has underlying vector space $A\\otimes_kB$, parity $(A\\widehat\\otimes B)^r=\\bigoplus_{i+j=r}A^i\\otimes_kB^j$, and multiplication\n\n$$\n(a\\otimes b)(a'\\otimes b')=(-1)^{|b||a'|}(aa'\\otimes bb')\n$$\n\nfor homogeneous factors, extended by the finite sum\n\n$$\n\\sum_{i,j,r,s\\in\\{0,1\\}}(-1)^{jr}(a_i a'_r\\otimes b_j b'_s),\\qquad a=\\sum_i a_i,\\ b=\\sum_j b_j,\\ a'=\\sum_r a'_r,\\ b'=\\sum_s b'_s.\n$$\n\nEach parity projection is linear, so this formula is $k$-multilinear in the four inputs and therefore defines a multiplication on $(A\\otimes_kB)\\times(A\\otimes_kB)$ by [[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]].           "statement": "Let $\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ be the real algebra for the form with $p$ positive and $q$ negative squares, using $v^2=Q(v)1$. As ungraded real algebras, for $p,q,n\\ge0$,\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_{p+1,q+1}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}M_2(\\mathbb R),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{n+2,0}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}M_2(\\mathbb R),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+2}\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}\\otimes_{\\mathbb R}\\mathbb H.$$\n\nThe pure-signature algebras through dimension eight are\n\n| $n$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ |\n|---:|---|---|\n| $0$ | $\\mathbb R$ | $\\mathbb R$ |\n| $1$ | $\\mathbb R\\oplus\\mathbb R$ | $\\mathbb C$ |\n| $2$ | $M_2(\\mathbb R)$ | $\\mathbb H$ |\n| $3$ | $M_2(\\mathbb C)$ | $\\mathbb H\\oplus\\mathbb H$ |\n| $4$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $5$ | $M_2(\\mathbb H)\\oplus M_2(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_4(\\mathbb C)$ |\n| $6$ | $M_4(\\mathbb H)$ | $M_8(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $7$ | $M_8(\\mathbb C)$ | $M_8(\\mathbb R)\\oplus M_8(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $8$ | $M_{16}(\\mathbb R)$ | $M_{16}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n\nFor every $n\\ge0$, the pure algebras satisfy\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_{n+8,0}\\cong M_{16}(\\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}),\\qquad \\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+8}\\cong M_{16}(\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}).$$",

          "source_path": "items/thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification.md",
          "statement": "Let $n=p+q$, let $r$ be the residue of $p-q$ modulo $8$ in $\\{0,1,\\ldots,7\\}$, and use $v^2=Q(v)1$ with signature ordered $(+^p,-^q)$. For every nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$, the real Clifford algebra is\n\n| $r$ | parity of $n$ | $\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ |\n|---:|:---:|---|\n| $0$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $1$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb R)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $2$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb R)$ |\n| $3$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)$ |\n| $4$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $5$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\\mathbb H)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $6$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\\mathbb H)$ |\n| $7$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)$ |\n\nOnly signatures with $p,q\\ge0$ are considered; in the feasible rows the displayed exponents are nonnegative. For a nondegenerate complex quadratic form on dimension $n$, its Clifford algebra is\n\n$$\\mathrm{Cl}_n(\\mathbb C)\\cong\\begin{cases}M_{2^{n/2}}(\\mathbb C),&n\\text{ even},\\\\M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C)\\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\\mathbb C),&n\\text{ odd}.\\end{cases}$$\n\nThese matrix-algebra classifications require nondegeneracy; no such classification is asserted for degenerate forms.",

          "source_path": "items/thm-graded-clifford-modules-and-real-complex-types.md",
          "statement": "Let $A=\\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ be a positive-dimensional standard real Clifford algebra with the canonical grading from [[lem-clifford-quotient-has-canonical-z2-grading]], and write $A^0$ for its even subalgebra. If $p>0$ then $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{q,p-1}$, and if $p=0$ then $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,q-1}$. For the standard complex Clifford algebra in dimension $n>0$, $A^0\\cong\\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n-1}(\\mathbb C)$. Here an irreducible graded module means a nonzero graded module with no proper nonzero graded submodule ([[def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product]]). Its isomorphism class, with parity-preserving maps, is exactly the class of a simple left $A^0$-module under the induction correspondence of [[thm-graded-module-classification-from-even-subalgebra]].\n\nConsequently, if the applicable even-algebra entry in [[thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification]] is $M_m(D)$, there is one irreducible graded module with even part the column module $D^m$; if it is $M_m(D)\\oplus M_m(D)$, there are two, one supported on each factor. Their coefficient type is $D\\in\\{\\mathbb R,\\mathbb C,\\mathbb H\\}$. In complex scalars the type is always $\\mathbb C$. At dimension zero, the algebra is purely even and has two irreducible graded modules, concentrated in parity $0$ and parity $1$, respectively.\n\nFor standard complex $\\mathrm{Cl}_n(\\mathbb C)$ with $n=2m>0$, the normalized volume element $\\omega=i^m e_1\\cdots e_n$ has square $1$, lies in the even subalgebra, and anticommutes with every odd generator. The two graded-module classes are the two choices of which $\\omega$-eigenspace is placed in parity $0$; these are the two chiral parity conventions. For $n=2m+1$, the same formula gives an odd central element with square $1$; its two central idempotents are exchanged by the grading, so the two ungraded simple factors pair into the unique graded-simple class.",

          "deps": [
            "def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism",

          ],
          "dependency_level": 7,
          "statement": "Let $f:W\\to Z$ be a filtered L∞-morphism as in [[def-filtered-l-infinity-morphism]], and put $P=F^1W$, $P'=F^1Z$. On $C(P)=\\bigoplus_{n\\ge0}S^nP$, including $S^0P=k\\cdot1$, use the symmetric multiplication and the counital coproduct\n\n$$\\Delta(x_1\\cdots x_n)=\\sum_{I\\sqcup J=\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}}\\epsilon(I,J;x)x_I\\otimes x_J.$$\n\nEmpty subsets are allowed. Define $\\mathcal F^NC(P)$ as the span of products $x_1\\cdots x_n$ with $x_j\\in F^{i_j}W$, all $i_j\\ge1$, and $\\sum_j i_j\\ge N$; scalars have weight zero. Define the **completed coaugmented symmetric coalgebra**\n\n$$\\widehat C(P)=\\varprojlim_N C(P)/\\mathcal F^NC(P).$$\n\nAll completions and limits are degreewise. Complete tensor products for coproducts with the sum of the two weight filtrations. Then multiplication, coproduct, counit and coaugmentation extend continuously, as do $Q$ and the Taylor map $F$. Their continuous extensions satisfy $Q^2=0$, $\\Delta F=(F\\widehat\\otimes F)\\Delta$, and $FQ=RF$. The length-one projection extends continuously to $p_P:\\widehat C(P)\\to P$.\n\nFor $w\\in P^0$ and homogeneous $v\\in F^pW$, $p\\ge1$, define the convergent expressions\n\n$$e^w=\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\frac{w^n}{n!},\\qquad c_q(w)=\\sum_{n\\ge1}\\frac{q_n(w^n)}{n!},\\qquad u=f_*(w)=\\sum_{n\\ge1}\\frac{f_n(w^n)}{n!}.$$\n\nThey satisfy\n\n$$\\Delta e^w=e^w\\otimes e^w,\\qquad e^we^{-w}=1,\\qquad Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w,\\qquad F(e^w)=e^u,$$\n\nand the marked-input identity\n\n$$F(ve^w)=\\left(\\sum_{n\\ge0}\\frac{f_{n+1}(w^n,v)}{n!}\\right)e^u.$$\n\nThis is a total filtration weight completion on the positive-filtration subalgebra, not an unspecified product by symmetric arity on all of $W$."

          "statement": "Let $\\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, let $B$ be the invariant form normalized so long roots have square $2$, and let $\\mathfrak k$ be a compact real form. The adjoint action of the Casimir $\\Omega_B$ from [[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]] is a unique positive scalar $\\gamma_B$ times the identity."
        },
        {
          "id": "def-dual-coxeter-number-for-normalized-form",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Dual Coxeter number for the normalized invariant form",
          "dependency_level": 0,

        {
          "id": "lem-sugawara-quadratic-modes-well-defined",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "Restricted Sugawara quadratic mode sums are well defined",

          ],
          "statement": "A skew central cocycle supported on m+n=0 and normalized by a(1,-1)=0 has a(m,-m)=c(m^3-m)/12."
        },
        {
          "id": "lem-witt-cubic-cocycle-is-a-2-cocycle",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "The cubic Witt cocycle is a Lie-algebra two-cocycle",

          "statement": "For omega(d_m,d_n)=delta_(m+n,0)(m^3-m)/12, prove alternatingness and the cyclic Lie-algebra two-cocycle identity."

          "statement": "For level k with k+h^vee nonzero, define L_m=(2(k+h^vee))^-1 sum_a sum_r :J_a(r)J^a(m-r):, with the chosen dual-basis and positive-energy normal-ordering convention."

            "def-dual-coxeter-number-for-normalized-form",

          "statement": "Let $V$ be any restricted affine-current module of level $k\\in\\mathbb C$ as in [[def-positive-energy-affine-module]], for a finite-dimensional complex simple $\\mathfrak g$ with normalized invariant form $B$. Put $q=k+h^\\vee\\ne0$ and use [[def-sugawara-modes]]. Then for every $x\\in\\mathfrak g$ and $m,n\\in\\mathbb Z$,\n$$[L_m,J_x(n)]=-nJ_x(m+n).$$\nNo grading, inner product, irreducibility, or integrability of $V$ is required."
        },

          "id": "lem-sugawara-modes-act-on-currents",
          "kind": "lemma",

For the modes of [[def-sugawara-modes]], every $x\\in\\mathfrak g$ and $m,n\\in\\mathbb Z$ satisfy\n$$[L_m,J_x(n)]=-nJ_x(m+n).$$\nIn particular this holds on all positive-energy unitary modules in the previously considered nonnegative integral level branch."

          "title": "Sugawara modes satisfy Virasoro at every noncritical complex level",
          "dependency_level": 5,

            "lem-sugawara-modes-act-on-currents",
            "def-positive-energy-affine-module",
            "def-untwisted-affine-central-extension",
            "def-virasoro-algebra"
          ],
          "statement": "Let $\\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra with invariant form $B$ normalized so long roots have square $2$. On every restricted affine-current module $V$ of complex level $k\\ne-h^\\vee$ as in [[def-positive-energy-affine-module]], the operators of [[def-sugawara-modes]] satisfy\n$$[L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+\\frac{c}{12}(m^3-m)\\delta_{m+n,0}I_V,\\qquad c=\\frac{k\\dim\\mathfrak g}{k+h^\\vee}.$$\nConsequently these operators and $C\\mapsto cI_V$ define a representation of [[def-virasoro-algebra]]. No energy grading, unitarity, irreducibility or integrability is assumed. The critical level is excluded from this normalized formula."
        }

          ],
          "statement": "A homotopy type $X$ is **locally finite** if every homotopy group $\\pi_i(X,x)$ is finite for every point $x$, and for each $x$ there is an integer $n_x$ such that $\\pi_i(X,x)=0$ for $i>n_x$.\n\nWrite $\\pi_0(X)$ for the set of connected components. Let $\\mathbb Q_c(X)$ be the rational-valued functions on $\\pi_0(X)$ with finite support. For a component $x$, the **homotopy weight** is\n$$\nw_X(x):=\\prod_{i>0}|\\pi_i(X,x)|^{(-1)^i}.\n$$\nThe product is finite because the positive homotopy groups vanish in high degrees; a negative exponent means a reciprocal.\n\nFor a map $f:X\\to Y$ of locally finite homotopy types and $\\alpha\\in\\mathbb Q_c(X)$, define\n$$\nf_!(\\alpha)(y):=\\sum_{x\\in\\pi_0(F_y)}\\alpha(i_y(x))\\,w_{F_y}(x),\n$$\nwhere $F_y$ is the homotopy fiber of $f$ at $y$ ([[def-homotopy-fiber-of-a-map]]) and $i_y:F_y\\to X$ is its natural map. For a proper map, meaning one whose homotopy fibers have finitely many connected components, also define $f^*:\\mathbb Q_c(Y)\\to\\mathbb Q_c(X)$ by $f^*\\beta=\\beta\\circ\\pi_0(f)$.\n\nThe ratio lemma [[lem-homotopy-fiber-component-weight-ratio]] proves that fibers of maps between locally finite homotopy types are locally finite and that the displayed sum is finite.         {
          "id": "lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "Nonvanishing of an entire quantum-binomial row and the characteristic digits",
          "deps": [
            "def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic",

          "justified_by": [],
          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion.md",
          "statement": "For $0\\le k\\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\\sum_w Q^{\\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\\in\\mathbb Z[T]$ such that\n\n$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$\n\nIt agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.\n\nFor a field $K$, $\\delta\\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\\ell$, and $p=\\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\\delta)$ for $0\\le k\\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\\ell=\\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\\ge1$ and $1\\le a<p$; if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.",
          "dependency_level": 1
        },
        {
          "id": "lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-representation-is-split-injective",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "The integral two-letter Temperley–Lieb representation has a linear left inverse",
          "deps": [
            "def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category",
            "thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws",
            "thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-generators-span",
            "def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis"
          ],
          "justified_by": [],
          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-representation-is-split-injective.md",
          "statement": "Put $A=\\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $\\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$, let $V_n$ be the free $R$-module on binary words of length $n$, with $V_0=R$. The cup and cap maps are\n\n$$c(1)=q(01)+(10),\\qquad b(01)=1,\\quad b(10)=q^{-1},\\quad b(00)=b(11)=0.$$\n\nInsertion of these maps in adjacent positions defines a representation\n\n$$\\rho_n:\\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\\delta)\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{End}_R(V_n).$$\n\nOver $A$ this map has an $A$-linear left inverse, and the same left inverse works after every base change to $R$. In particular, it is injective over every such $R$. It preserves the number of ones, and on the local ordered basis $00,01,10,11$ the generator $d_i$ has zero $00,11$ blocks and middle block\n\n$$\\begin{pmatrix}q&1\\\\1&q^{-1}\\end{pmatrix}.$$\n\nHorizontal reflection of an endomorphism diagram is represented by matrix transpose.",
          "dependency_level": 3
        },
        {
          "id": "lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-quantum-binomial-criterion-over-fields",
          "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "Jones–Wenzl existence over a field is detected by one quantum-binomial row",
          "deps": [
            "def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category",
            "thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-category-laws",
            "thm-temperley-lieb-diagram-generators-span",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-generators-satisfy-local-relations",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-projector-exists-iff-trivial-projective",
            "def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-integral-spin-representation-is-split-injective",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion",
            "thm-irreducible-quotient-adjoins-a-root"
          ],
          "justified_by": [],
          "source_path": "items/lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-quantum-binomial-criterion-over-fields.md",
          "statement": "Let $K$ be a field, $\\delta\\in K$, and $n\\ge0$. A normalized idempotent $e\\in\\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\\delta)$ with $d_ie=0$ for $1\\le i<n$ exists if and only if every $B_{n,k}(\\delta)$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]], $0\\le k\\le n$, is nonzero. Every such $e$ also satisfies $ed_i=0$ and is unique. This is a field assertion; it makes no integral-ring descent claim.",
          "dependency_level": 4
        },
        {
          "id": "thm-temperley-lieb-spencer-jones-wenzl-existence-criterion",
          "kind": "theorem",
          "title": "Spencer's quantum-characteristic criterion for Jones–Wenzl existence",
          "deps": [
            "def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-quantum-binomial-criterion-over-fields",
            "lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion"
          ],
          "justified_by": [],
          "dependency_level": 5,
          "statement": "Let $K$ be a field, $\\delta\\in K$, let $\\ell$ be the quantum characteristic from [[def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic]], and let $p=\\operatorname{char}K$ (write $p=\\infty$ in characteristic zero). A normalized idempotent $e\\in\\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\\delta)$ satisfying $\\varepsilon(e)=1$ and $d_i e=0$ for every $1\\le i<n$ exists exactly in the following cases:\n\n1. if $\\ell=\\infty$, every finite $n$ satisfies the criterion $n<\\ell$;\n2. if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p$ is finite, then $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\,p(i)-1$ for some $i\\ge1$ and integer $1\\le a<p$;\n3. if $\\ell<\\infty$ and $p=\\infty$, then $n<\\ell$ or $n=a\\ell-1$ for some positive integer $a$.\n\nThe criterion is over fields. It does not assert descent to an arbitrary coefficient ring."
        }
      ],

          "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf\nsuppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine\nalgebraic group, $B\\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus,\n$X=G/B$, $\\mathfrak g=\\operatorname{Lie}G$,\n$\\mathfrak h=\\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by\n$B$. Write $\\rho=\\frac12\\sum_{\\alpha\\in\\Phi^+}\\alpha$. All schemes are over\n$\\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\\eta$, $\\mathcal O_X(\\eta)$ denotes the\n$G$-equivariant line bundle $G\\times^B\\mathbb C_\\eta$ with fiber character\n$\\eta$ at $eB$.\n\nThe infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor\n$$a_X:\\mathcal L_X:=\\mathcal O_X\\otimes_{\\mathbb C}\\mathfrak g\\longrightarrow T_X,\\qquad f\\otimes x\\longmapsto f x_X.$$\nGive $\\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket\n$$[f\\otimes x,g\\otimes y]=fg\\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\\otimes y-g y_X(f)\\otimes x.$$\nIts kernel $\\mathfrak b_X=\\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at\n$gB$ its fiber is $\\operatorname{Ad}(g)\\mathfrak b$.\n\nFor any $\\kappa\\in\\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\\kappa+\\rho$ of\n$\\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an\n$\\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\\chi^X_{\\kappa+\\rho}:\\mathfrak b_X\\to\\mathcal O_X$.\nThe transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a\ncharacter is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$.
