          "statement": "Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\\vee},v)$ be a finite-type symmetrizable Cartan datum, with\n$v_i=v^{d_i}$, and let $U_v(\\mathfrak g)$ be the scalar extension of\n[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from $\\mathbb Q(v)$ to\n$\\mathbb C(v)$. The finite-type Lie algebra $\\mathfrak g$ is the Serre Lie\nalgebra of the matrix $A$\n([[def-serre-lie-algebra-of-a-finite-type-cartan-matrix]]). Write\n$A_L=\\mathbb C[v,v^{-1}]$ and\n$A_{DK}=\\mathbb C[v,v^{-1},(v_i-v_i^{-1})^{-1}\\ (i\\in I)]$.\n\nThe **Lusztig divided-power form** $U^L_{A_L}(\\mathfrak g)$ is the scalar\nextension to $A_L$ of the subalgebra $U_A$ defined in\n[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]. Thus it is generated by the\ndivided powers $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)}$, the toral elements $K_h^{\\pm1}$, and the\ntoral quantum binomials $T_{i,c,t}$.\n\nThe **De Concini–Kac form** $U^{DK}_{A_{DK}}(\\mathfrak g)$ is the\n$A_{DK}$-subalgebra of $U_v(\\mathfrak g)$ generated by $E_i,F_i$ and\n$K_h^{\\pm1}$. It uses ordinary powers of the root generators. This definition\ndoes not assert that it is free over $A_{DK}$ or that its later specialization\nembeds into the Lusztig specialization.\n\nLet $\\zeta\\in\\mathbb C^\\times$ be a root of unity. Require\n$\\zeta_i-\\zeta_i^{-1}\\ne0$ for each $i$ and put\n$\\ell_i=\\operatorname{ord}(\\zeta_i^2)>1$. The specialization map sends\n$v\\mapsto\\zeta$ and has target $\\mathbb C$. Define\n$$U^{DK}_\\zeta(\\mathfrak g):=U^{DK}_{A_{DK}}(\\mathfrak g)\\otimes_{A_{DK},\\,v\\mapsto\\zeta}\\mathbb C,\\qquad U^L_\\zeta(\\mathfrak g):=U^L_{A_L}(\\mathfrak g)\\otimes_{A_L,\\,v\\mapsto\\zeta}\\mathbb C.$$\nIn the standard good odd-order branch, $\\zeta$ has odd order $\\ell$ and\n$\\ell$ is relatively prime to every $d_i$; then every $\\ell_i=\\ell$.\n\nA root-power quotient depends on the chosen toral lattice. In the\nconvention where the torus is generated by the $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$, define\nthe **simple-root-power candidate** $u_\\zeta^{\\mathrm{cand}}(\\mathfrak g)$ as the quotient of that ordinary-generator De Concini–Kac algebra by the\ntwo-sided ideal generated by\n$E_i^{\\ell_i},F_i^{\\ell_i},K_i^{\\ell_i}-1$ for $i\\in I$. This names the quotient construction only. In higher rank it is not the definition of the standard small quantum group: nonsimple positive-root powers need not be killed by imposing only the displayed simple-root powers. No finite dimension, embedding, or higher-rank identification is asserted for this candidate. The rank-one results below use this quotient, where there are no nonsimple positive roots, and denote it by $u_\\zeta(\\mathfrak{sl}_2)$.\n\nFor a standard **small image form**, let $D_\\zeta^{(i)}$ be the specialization of the ordinary-generator form with torus generated by the $K_i^{\\pm1}$. Define\n$$\\overline U^L_\\zeta=U^L_\\zeta/(K_h^\\ell-1:h\\in P^\\vee),\\qquad \\overline u_\\zeta=\\operatorname{im}\\bigl(D_\\zeta^{(i)}\\longrightarrow\\overline U^L_\\zeta\\bigr)$$\nin the good odd-order branch. The map is the specialization of the generic inclusion into the divided-power form localized by the invertible $v_i-v_i^{-1}$, followed by the toral quotient; it is well defined because those denominators are nonzero at the chosen root. This image definition fixes the actual ordinary-generator form without claiming a presentation by simple root-power relations. The general dimension and root-vector PBW description require separate proofs; no such assertion is implicit here.\n\nThe generic inclusion of the ordinary-generator form into the divided-power\nform does not by itself assert an inclusion after specializing $v$. The\nrank-one items on this page prove a specific root-power quotient and exhibit\nthe failure of injectivity after specialization. This definition does not\nassert a quantum Frobenius theorem or any generic-$v$ semisimplicity at a root\nof unity.",

          "statement": "Let $\\Phi$ be a finite simply-laced root system in its real root span, with positive roots $\\Phi^+$, root lattice $Q$, Weyl group $W$ and $(\\alpha,\\alpha)=2$.           "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "Let $R=(X,\\Phi,Y,\\Phi^\\vee,\\Delta)$ be a reduced based root datum: $X,Y$ are finite-rank free lattices in perfect integral duality, $\\Phi\\subset X$ is the finite root set, $\\Phi^\\vee\\subset Y$ its coroot set, $\\Delta$ a base, and $W_0$ the finite Weyl group ([[def-abstract-root-datum-and-its-weyl-group]]). Its finite simple-reflection set is $S_0:=\\{s_\\alpha:\\alpha\\in\\Delta\\}\\subset W_0$; the simple reflections in a chosen base generate $W_0$ ([[lem-root-datum-combinatorics]]). Write $Q^\\vee=\\mathbb Z\\Phi^\\vee\\subseteq Y$ for the coroot lattice.\n\nPut $V=Y\\otimes_\\mathbb Z\\mathbb R$. The **canonical affine walls** are $H_{\\alpha,j}=\\{v:\\langle\\alpha,v\\rangle=j\\}$, with reflection $r_{\\alpha,j}(v)=v-(\\langle\\alpha,v\\rangle-j)\\alpha^\\vee$. The base alcove $A$ is the unique alcove in the positive chamber with $0$ in its closure; equivalently $A$ is defined by $0<\\langle\\alpha,v\\rangle<1$ for every positive root $\\alpha$. If there are no roots, put $A=V$. For a nonsemisimple root datum the alcoves include the whole common root kernel as a factor. Define $W_{\\mathrm{aff}}=Q^\\vee\\rtimes W_0$, let $S_{\\mathrm{aff}}$ be its reflections in the walls of $A$, put $W_{\\mathrm e}=Y\\rtimes W_0$, and let $\\Omega=\\operatorname{Stab}_{W_{\\mathrm e}}(A)$. The canonical affine Coxeter system and the decomposition $W_{\\mathrm e}=W_{\\mathrm{aff}}\\rtimes\\Omega$, including central lattice directions, are proved in [[lem-hh-root-datum-affine-geometry-and-wall-parameters]]. In particular $S_0\\subset S_{\\mathrm{aff}}$ with the finite Weyl product orders. Define length on $W_{\\mathrm e}$ as the number of walls separating $A$ from its translate; on $W_{\\mathrm{aff}}$ it is Coxeter length, and its zero set is $\\Omega$. Thus no arbitrary nongeometric affine Coxeter extension is silently compared with the lattice below.\n\nChoose a parameter function $q:S_{\\mathrm{aff}}\\to\\mathbb R_{>0}$ invariant under conjugation by $W_{\\mathrm e}$. For $s,t\\in S_{\\mathrm{aff}}$ with finite Coxeter label $m(s,t)$, impose the alternating braid relation with $m(s,t)$ factors. Thus it adjoins symbols $U_\\omega$ with $U_\\omega U_\\eta=U_{\\omega\\eta}$ and $U_\\omega T_sU_\\omega^{-1}=T_{\\omega s\\omega^{-1}}$.
